docs.title: phiward
docs.text:
phiward keeps protected health information (PHI) and your credentials out of what an AI coding agent sends to its model provider. The agent's tools send their output to the provider, and that output can hold file contents, sample identifiers or file names. With phiward, the agent works on protected data only through a gateway that masks names and identifiers.

  • Status: v0.2.0b1, a beta. See the release notes.
  • Needs: macOS or Linux, and Claude Code 2.1.295 or newer.
  • Install: uv tool install --python-preference only-managed phiward==0.2.0b1, then the quick start.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A["The agent's tools: Read, Grep, Bash, MCP"] --> B{"A protected folder or a credential?"}
  B -->|"no"| P["Reaches the model provider as before"]
  B -->|"yes"| R["Refused by phiward's hook and the sandbox"]
  R --> Q["Only the refusal and its reason reach the provider"]
  A --> G["Work on protected data: phiward run or phiward copy"]
  G --> K["Your broker runs it outside the agent, in a kernel sandbox"]
  K --> M["The output, with names and identifiers masked"]

Masking hides names and identifiers, not other content. Through the gateway, print counts and summaries, not records.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: This page lists every config key, file place and environment variable. For a first setup, use phiward setup (setup.md); it writes the keys that matter most.

docs.title: Where the files are
docs.text:
phiward reads two files and combines them.

File Place Who writes it Commit it? User config $PHIWARD_CONFIG, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/phiward/config.toml, else ~/.config/phiward/config.toml the operator (phiward setup, or by hand) no Repo config .phiward.toml, the first one found from the working folder upward the repository's maintainers (the agent can edit it too) yes

With no config and no protected paths, the guards do nothing. If $PHIWARD_CONFIG names a file that does not exist, the config is bad (see Fail closed).

phiward also uses these places. You do not configure them in a file.

Place What it is The agent may ~/.cache/phiward (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/phiward) the gateway's scratch folders, while commands run not read or write it ~/.phiward-spool (or $PHIWARD_SPOOL) requests from clients to the broker write requests (it must) ~/.phiward/broker.json the broker's status: the config, cache folder, roots and patterns it uses not write it ~/.phiward/backups/keys the keys of phiward pseudonymize (ID, a tab, the code), mode 0700; made on first use inside ~/.phiward/backups, which install makes not read or write it

docs.title: Who may set what
docs.text:
The agent can edit a repo config, and it chooses the folder that a gateway request comes from. So a repo config may only add protection. Everything that widens or changes what a gateway command can do comes from the user config only.

Key User config Repo config [protected_paths] roots, patterns yes yes, adds (the gateway cannot write a repo-only root) [protected_paths] unresolved yes only stricter [protected_paths] snapshot_names yes yes, adds [sanitize] packs yes (built-in names and pack files) built-in names only; pack files are ignored [sanitize] names_from, patterns, subjects yes ignored [sanitize] inventory_limit yes only lower [copy] remotes, ssh_config, push_limit_gib yes ignored [sanitize] table, id_columns yes ignored [remote] hosts, commands, roots, use_shared_connection yes ignored [launch] pass_env yes ignored [broker] write_to, net yes ignored [network] limit, allowed_domains yes ignored [broker] commands yes narrows: a program must be in every list that is set [broker] max_output_lines yes only lower [git] protected_branches yes yes, adds [shell] best_effort yes ignored

A repo config that sets an ignored key is not an error. phiward doctor lists the ignored keys.

docs.title: Every key
docs.text:
An example user config with every key:

[protected_paths]
# Folders that the agent must never read. Absolute, or starting with ~/ or $HOME.
# No "..", no "$" variable other than $HOME (or ${HOME}), no wildcard (* ? [).
# Each should exist.
roots = ["~/data/patients", "~/data/study-a"]

# Glob patterns for protected places. Absolute, or starting with ~/ or $HOME. "*" matches inside
# one path part ("?" and "[...]" are refused).
# Prefer roots: Claude Code's sandbox cannot take patterns.
patterns = ["~/projects/*/inputs/patient"]

# More folder names that hold snapshots of a root (protected too). The usual ones (.snapshot,
# .snapshots, .zfs, ~snapshot) are always found.
snapshot_names = [".backups"]

# What the hook's text check does with a variable it cannot see: "allow", "ask" or "deny".
# Default "deny". Used only where the shell is not kernel-confined.
unresolved = "deny"

[sanitize]
# Pattern packs. A name without "/" is a built-in pack ("genomics", "msk", "dates").
# A name with "/" is the path of your own pack file. Default ["genomics"].
packs = ["genomics"]

# Index files whose paths hold names to mask (<NAME>): lines of tab-separated fields; each
# field with a "/" is a path, and its parts (and their dash pieces) are masked. Keep the files
# inside a protected root: the list is protected data, and elsewhere the agent can read it.
names_from = ["~/data/patients/.names.txt"]

# Extra rules, each 'REGEX => <PLACEHOLDER>'.
patterns = ['\bPT-\d{6}\b => <SAMPLEID>']

# Or your record that the protected data holds no subject or sample IDs beyond the names
# under the roots (phiward doctor warns until a rule masks them or this is set):
# subjects = "none"

# The most entries the sanitizer lists under the roots. Default 200000.
inventory_limit = 200000

# Whether `phiward run --table` may be used (it lets numbers through in columns not named as
# identifiers). Default false.
table = false
# More column headers whose cells `phiward run --table` masks whole, added to the built-in list.
id_columns = ["lab_code", "Visit-Code"]

[copy]
# Places on other machines that `phiward copy` may copy to or from: "host:/absolute/prefix".
remotes = ["cluster:/data/work/study-a"]
# The ssh config every HPC request uses (it names the host's ControlPath; see hpc.md).
ssh_config = "~/.config/phiward/ssh_config"
# A push larger than this many GiB is refused: copy it yourself. Default 5.
push_limit_gib = 5

[remote]
# Hosts `phiward run --remote` may name, programs it may run there, protected paths there
# (masked in remote output; a push goes only under one).
hosts = ["cluster"]
commands = ["squeue", "sacct", "sinfo"]
roots = ["/data/protected", "/data/work/study-a"]
# Join your shared SSH connection (no request reads a key or ticket). Default true.
use_shared_connection = true

[launch]
# Extra environment variables passed to a `phiward launch` session (the agent can read them).
pass_env = []

[broker]
# Folders where `phiward run --write-to DIR` may write (DIR is one of them or inside one).
# Each must be a real, existing folder. Default: none.
write_to = ["~/projects/study-a/results"]

# Whether `phiward run --net` gets the network. Default false.
net = false

# The most lines of a gateway command's output that the agent sees. Default 2000.
max_output_lines = 2000
# The programs gateway commands may run (default: any). Set it for real patient data. A listed
# program starts in a private folder, not in the agent's: paths are given in full.
# commands = ["@genomics", "~/pipelines/bin/"]

[git]
# Branches that `git push` must not change (the pre-push hook).
protected_branches = ["main", "release"]

[network]
# Shell commands in Claude Code sessions reach only these hosts (Mode A). Default false.
limit = true
allowed_domains = ["github.com", "pypi.org"]

[shell]
# Take the hook's text check where Claude Code's sandbox does not confine the shell. Default
# false: then such a shell runs only gateway calls.
best_effort = false

docs.title: [protected_paths]
docs.text:
• roots (list of folders). Claude Code's sandbox (as install writes it) denies the agent's shell every read and write of each root, and the hook refuses the file tools. The gateway can read every root. It writes only in [broker] write_to folders, which may sit inside a root.
  • patterns (list of globs). Like roots, for places that are spread out. * matches any run of characters in one path part, names that start with a dot included; it is the only wildcard. ?, [...] and any character outside printable ASCII are refused (the config is then bad, and the message suggests a rewrite): give such names as roots. On macOS, letter case does not matter. Every part of phiward (hook, the gateway and launch profiles, sanitizer, settings check) uses this one meaning. On Linux, Claude Code's sandbox cannot hold patterns, so with patterns the hook refuses shell commands other than gateway calls; the gateway and launch cover the folders that match when they start. A match reached through a link is neither hidden on that path nor a gateway write place.
  • snapshot_names (list of folder names). Snapshot folders next to a root or above it hold old copies of protected files. .snapshot, .snapshots, .zfs and ~snapshot are found without this key; add your site's name here if it differs. Each one found becomes a protected folder. A repo config may add names too (it only adds protection). On Linux, other mounts of the same file system that show a root (bind mounts, a second mount of one share) are protected the same way.
  • unresolved ("allow", "ask" or "deny"; default "deny"). Where the shell is not kernel-confined, the hook checks command text only. This is what it does with a $VARIABLE or text it cannot parse. When the tool cannot ask (Claude Code in a bypass or "don't ask" mode), "ask" becomes a deny.

docs.title: [sanitize]
docs.text:
The sanitizer filters everything a gateway command prints, the output of phiward sanitize, and what the git hooks check. It always masks protected paths (<PROTECTED>). For run and copy it also masks the name of every entry under the roots (<ENTRY>); sanitize and the git hooks do not list the roots, so they do not. These keys add to that.

In text mode (without --table) the genomics pack masks positions and long numbers (<LOCUS>, <NUM>, for example any run of 5 or more digits, also next to a comma). A run joined to other digits by a dot keeps its digits, as in a decimal (12345.678, but also 1234567.7654321). phiward run --table reads CSV or TSV output by column instead, one table per output. The header is the first non-empty line, when it has 2 or more fields split by tabs (else by commas), each with a letter or _ first (after an optional #), no quote, no run of 3 digits and nothing a rule masks, and when at least one of its columns is an identifier column (the built-in list or id_columns, below). Otherwise the whole output is text, so a table without an identifier column keeps no numbers under --table, and neither does output whose first line is a warning or prose (Results, see below). Ordinary data can still pass these tests: a first line that holds an identifier word (a row of data printed without its header, as by tail -n +2 x.tsv, or prose such as sample, mrn) is read as a header, and the numbers in its other columns are kept. Under the header, each row is first masked on the whole line as in table mode (protected paths, entry names, identifier rules, names). Then a cell under an identifier header (the built-in list or id_columns, below) shows <IDCOL>, whatever its shape. A cell of another column keeps a plain number (7654321, 12.5, 1e-05, 1,234,567); any other text in it gets the position rules (chr1:1234567 is <LOCUS>). The first line that is not such a row ends column mode: it and every later line are masked as text. Such a line is an empty line, a row with another field count, a quote, a backslash or a %XX escape, a row with no plain-number cell (another header, as from cat a.csv b.csv, or a row of words such as TP53,BRCA1), and a line too long to read. Output without a header line, or with a line before it (a warning on stderr too), is all text. When no header was found, the output ends with a note that says so. Rules that span cells in text mode do not match cell by cell: under chrom and pos, chr1 and 1234567 are both shown. So a record number in a column whose header is not on the list would pass: --table is off unless you turn it on with table = true (user config only). Turn it on only when identifiers in your data are caught by a pack, a pattern or a column header, not by the number rule. phiward sanitize --table and the git hooks read no columns: they mask each line as in table mode (identifiers only; numbers and positions are kept).

An entry name shorter than 4 characters (6 when it is only digits) is not masked, and neither is one that is a common word of the built-in stop list (for example patient, normal, tumour, bam, runs, test).

  • packs (list). Built-in packs are genomics (the default) and msk (one institution's identifiers; an example, not a default). A pack file has the lists paths, identifiers, positions and keep_files; the format is at the top of phiward/packs/genomics.toml in the installed package. A pack file must be a regular file, not a link.
  • names_from (list of files). Index files: each line is tab-separated fields; in each field that holds a /, every path part of 4 or more characters, the part before its first dot, and its -/_/. pieces are masked as <NAME> (never a stop word or a bare number). A file must be a regular file, not a link. Keep these files inside a protected root: elsewhere the agent can read the list. --names-from FILE on run follows the same rules, and its file must be inside a protected path of the user config: the broker reads it outside the sandbox, and a file elsewhere would let the agent test what it holds.
  • table (true or false, default false; user config only). Whether --table may be used.
  • id_columns (list; user config only). Column headers whose cells phiward run --table masks whole, added to the built-in list (which cannot be shortened). Each entry is a header or a glob (*, ?, [...]) of at most 64 letters, digits, spaces and _ - . # * ? [ ] !. Headers and entries are compared in one form: spaces around them and one leading # removed, letter case ignored, and each run of spaces, - and . read as _. So "Patient ID" matches the headers Patient ID, patient-id and #PATIENT.ID. The built-in list: id, id*, *id, *_ids, *_id_*, pt, pt_*, *_pt, subj*, *sample*, *patient*, *subject*, *donor*, *mrn*, *barcode*, *accession*, *specimen*, *record*, *chart*, *encounter*, *visit*, *ssn*, *phone*, *zip*, *_no, *number*, case, case_*, *_case, *birth*, *dob*, *num, *nbr, *rec*, acc*, caseno, ptno, patno, labno, empi, fin, csn, participant*, individual*, proband*, person*, *date* (dates are identifiers too). It is broad on purpose: some numeric columns (n_samples, valid, records, read_number, accuracy, precision, direction, recall, update_date) show <IDCOL> too. Names it does not catch (HospNo, hn, kit, tube, a lab's own codes) belong in id_columns.
  • patterns (list). Each entry is REGEX => <PLACEHOLDER>. Like every identifier rule of a pack, it matches in any letter case; write (?-i:...) around a part that must keep its case. So the msk pack also masks some ordinary words (c-string, donor-derived), the git hook refuses a commit that holds them as it would an identifier, and phiward sanitize --check counts them. To check that your rules match your data, run a command over it: the note at the end of phiward run counts the placeholders shown and says when no identifier placeholder was shown.
  • subjects (user config only). Only "none": your record that the protected data holds no subject or sample identifiers beyond the names under the roots. Without it, and without a rule that masks them (the msk pack, a pack file of your own with an identifier rule whose placeholder is not <BAMFILE>, <READ> or <DATE>, patterns or names_from), phiward doctor warns. phiward setup asks; "none" is never its default. A repo config or a team template cannot set it.
  • inventory_limit (whole number, default 200000). The sanitizer lists every entry under the roots each time a gateway command starts. With more entries than this, it stops (fails closed). Raise it for a very large root, or narrow the root.

Built-in packs: genomics (the default), msk, and dates (v0.2, off by default: dates and times become <DATE>, for example the dates ls -l prints).

docs.title: [copy]
docs.text:
• remotes (list of host:/absolute/prefix). phiward copy may use a place under one of these as a source or a destination; a push lands only under a [remote] roots folder too. .. is refused. How pushes and pulls work: hpc.md.
  • push_limit_gib (whole number, default 5; user config only). A push larger than this is refused: copy it yourself.
  • ssh_config (a file; default none). The ssh config that every HPC request uses (ssh -F FILE, never ~/.ssh/config unless you name it), with the system ssh from /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin or /sbin, never from your PATH, and ProxyCommand, ProxyJump and LocalCommand off, BatchMode=yes. It must name the host's ControlPath (the shared connection, hpc.md). Keep it outside ~/.ssh; it becomes a guard file (the agent may not write it). An Include in it would read files the agent may write. The value must be absolute (or start with ~/).

docs.title: [remote]
docs.text: For phiward run --remote HOST -- CMD (hpc.md). User config only. - hosts (list): the hosts a remote run may name. - commands (list): the programs it may run there, as bare names. The default is empty, which refuses every remote run. Nothing confines a command on the remote side: this list is what limits its effects. - roots (list of absolute paths on the remote): masked in the output as <PROTECTED>. A push (phiward copy to a remote) goes only under one of these; with none, every push is refused. phiward setup makes each new copy remote's folder one. - use_shared_connection (true or false; default true). Every HPC request joins your shared SSH connection and reads no credential (hpc.md). false: ssh logs in itself, so requests can read your key or ticket and have the network.

docs.title: [launch]
docs.text: • pass_env (list): environment variables passed to a launched tool besides the built-in allow-list. The agent can read whatever you pass.

docs.title: [broker]
docs.text:
The grants. Nothing asks the operator at run time: what is not written here is refused.

  • write_to (list of folders; default none). With exactly one folder here, gateway commands may write in it without --write-to (the default results folder). phiward run --write-to DIR is allowed only when DIR resolves to one of these folders or a folder inside one. When the config loads, each entry is checked:
  • an entry that does not exist yet is skipped (doctor counts it);
  • an entry reached through a link is skipped (doctor counts it): whoever can change the link would choose the place. Name the real folder;
  • an entry that is /, the home folder or above it, in a dot-folder of the home folder, in ~/Library or a PATH folder, above a protected root, in a derived protected folder or a pattern match, that holds a names or pack file of the config, that holds a .claude folder, or that holds or is inside a phiward file or folder (the config, the code, the spool, the status file, the interpreter folder) is a problem: the config is bad.
  • an entry inside a protected root is fine: gateway commands write only in write_to folders (protected roots are read only for them), and what they write there stays protected.
  • net (true or false; default false). With true, phiward run --net gets the network. On macOS it may also look up DNS; local unix sockets stay blocked (an SSH agent's or a shared connection's socket would log in to HPC as you). On Linux it gets the host network (unix sockets stay blocked).
  • commands (list; default: not set, so any program may run). The programs that phiward run may run on protected data. An entry is:
  • a bare name: a program found on the broker's PATH by that name, called by that name (wc, not /usr/bin/wc);
  • @genomics or @counts: a built-in list (samtools, bedtools, tabix, bgzip, mosdepth, seqkit, wc, uniq, cut, du, checksums, ls, file, stat, head, tail, zcat, gzip, gunzip; @counts is the counting part). None of them runs other code it is given. fastqc, multiqc, bcftools and sort are left out on purpose: each can be told to start another program or load a library;
  • a path: one file, for example your own script, written as its real path: a path with a link on it lists nothing (phiward pin and doctor say so), because what is checked and what starts must be the same file. List a link by its name instead (a multi-call program such as busybox then acts as that name), or list its folder. A script's #! interpreter is not part of what you approve: point it at an interpreter the agent cannot change;
  • a folder (ending in /): every program in it, for example ~/pipelines/bin/, called by its path or its name in that folder (a link in the folder runs as that link, as in Homebrew's bin).

What runs is always the entry of your user config that lists it, never a link of the agent's: a repo config's list can only narrow yours.

When it is set, any other program is refused. You approve the listed programs as they are: phiward setup does it when it writes the config, and phiward pin does it again. The broker runs no listed program whose content differs from what you approved, and stops when one changes while it runs. After you update a listed program, check it and run phiward pin, then restart the broker. Approval covers every file of a listed folder and its subfolders, so keep a script's helpers there; a folder with more than 2000 files is never approved. Files and folders named by path, and listed programs you own, are protected from agent writes ((cd ~ && phiward install claude --user --write)). pin and doctor find the programs on the running broker's PATH, and name any that are new, changed or not installed. Set it when you work with real patient data: without it, code that the agent writes can run on protected data and print what it reads in a form masking does not catch (for example encoded). A program that runs other code it is given (an interpreter, a shell, git, find, xargs, make, sort, a workflow engine) undoes the list: list your own scripts, kept outside the projects the agent works in, instead. phiward doctor warns about such entries. A repo config may set its own list too; a program must then be in both. run --remote has its own list ([remote] commands). - max_output_lines (whole number, default 2000). The most lines of a gateway command's output (run, run --remote and copy) that the agent sees. The lines after that are counted, not shown, and a last line says how many were withheld. A notice such as [3 more identical line(s)] counts as a line; the placeholder note after the output does not, and counts only the lines shown. A repo config may only lower this value. To see more, write the results to a file in a write_to folder inside a protected root, and print a summary.

A grant gives code that the agent chooses that capability. To keep the gateway as closed as possible, leave write_to empty and net false (and [copy] remotes empty); this still is not a defence against a hijacked agent. See threat-model.md.

docs.title: [network]
docs.text:
The network of the shell commands that an agent runs in a Claude Code session (Mode A). With limit = true, (cd ~ && phiward install claude --user --write) writes Claude Code's own sandbox.network.strictAllowlist and allowedDomains into your user settings: shell commands then reach only the listed hosts, and are refused all others without a question. A repository's settings cannot add hosts or proxy ports (Claude Code ignores them while the user settings set strictAllowlist). They can still take a command out of the sandbox (sandbox.excludedCommands), and an excluded command reaches any host: phiward doctor warns then. Needs Claude Code 2.1.285 or newer.

Each listed host is a way out. Code the agent writes can send what it reads to any listed host, for example in a gist, an issue or a push to github.com. Claude Code's proxy decides by the host name the client gives, so a host behind a shared front (a CDN) can reach others behind it. A shared host by its exact name (raw.githubusercontent.com, s3.amazonaws.com) serves anyone's content, so it is a way out to every account behind it; phiward refuses only the wildcard forms. List only the hosts you need, and as narrowly as you can.

  • limit (true or false, default false). setup asks, and suggests yes for real data.
  • allowed_domains (list): the hosts shell commands may reach, for example github.com, *.pypi.org (every subdomain) or github.com:443 (one port). Not *, not a URL, and not a wildcard over a top-level or two-part public suffix (*.com, *.co.uk) or over, or below, a common shared hosting name where anyone can have a site (*.github.io, *.amazonaws.com, *.s3.amazonaws.com, *.vercel.app, ...). This is a short list, not the whole public suffix list: check a wildcard yourself. Empty: no host at all. Hosts of WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules in your user settings count too.

What it does not limit: Claude Code's own connection to the model provider, the WebFetch and WebSearch tools, MCP servers, hooks, and Mode B (phiward launch). install only adds: to remove a host, or to open the network again, edit sandbox.network in ~/.claude/settings.json yourself. phiward doctor shows how many hosts are open and names hosts in the settings that the config no longer lists.

docs.title: [git]
docs.text: • protected_branches (list). The pre-push hook refuses a push that changes or deletes one.

docs.title: Keys that are gone
docs.text:
Key Gone since What to do [broker] confirm 0.0.x Remove it. Grants are write_to and net. [broker] prompt 0.0.x Remove it. Nothing asks at run time.

A file that still sets one is a bad config, with a message that says this. phiward setup drops them.

docs.title: [shell]
docs.text:
[shell]
best_effort = true     # default false; user config only

A shell is confined when the kernel decides what its commands can read: Claude Code's sandbox, as install claude --user --write sets it. phiward doctor says whether it holds, and why not.

By default, phiward's hook refuses every command of a shell that is not confined. Only a phiward command written as the whole command runs there:

  • the gateway: phiward run -- CMD ... and phiward copy SRC... DST;
  • phiward doctor and phiward check -- CMD (check answers as if the command ran in the sandbox).

The refusal says how to fix it. This applies once protected paths are set; before the first setup, only the hidden list is checked, by the text check (best effort).

best_effort = true keeps the old behaviour: a shell command that no kernel confines gets the hook's text check instead of a refusal. That check cannot read shell text completely (threat model), so use it only where Claude Code's sandbox cannot run (GitHub Copilot, which runs phiward's hook without it; a Linux machine without a usable bubblewrap). For real data there, prefer phiward launch. doctor warns while it is on. Only your user config can set it.

[shell] strict and [shell] commands (strict mode, removed before release) still load and do nothing: the default refusal replaces strict mode. Remove them when you next edit the file.

docs.title: MCP servers
docs.text:
An MCP server is a program Claude Code starts, outside its sandbox, with your rights. phiward judges a server's tools by what confines them, not by guessing from their fields. phiward mcp list shows what each of your servers is and what to do about it; phiward mcp wrap NAME wraps one (modes.md).

  • A tool of a server wrapped in phiward launch -- runs in phiward's kernel profile: it works as usual, with the text check of its input. The hook trusts it as wrapped only while it really runs so: each phiward launch keeps a record of its own process, and the hook looks for a live one started with the entry's own id under its own Claude Code. So after phiward mcp wrap, start Claude Code again; /resume, /clear and compaction change nothing. A wrapped entry whose env sets PATH, HOME, PHIWARD_*, XDG_*, PYTHON*, LD_* or DYLD_*, or that has a cwd, counts as not wrapped: those change what runs. How the hook tells: threat-model.md.
  • A tool whose name says it runs commands on this machine (run_in_terminal, write_bash, run_command, execute_command, executeCode, start_process, run_python, send_keys, interact_with_process), from any other server or from Copilot, may make only one whole gateway call: one command (or cmd, script, input) string or one argv list, with no other options than a description, a title, a timeout (a number), a background flag (true or false) or this folder as cwd. Everything else is refused, and the refusal says what to do for that kind of server. JavaScript in a browser (a tool or server named for the browser: Chrome's execute_javascript) is not a shell, and neither is a name that only reads (read_terminal, search_shell_history) or a terminal tool given only a folder or a title (open_terminal_tab). A local query tool (execute_sql) is: a local database can run commands. Its remote server's tools work. Container exec (docker_exec) is a shell too. The desktop app's own _consent field (true or false) does not count as an option; any other field does.
  • With [shell] best_effort on, such a tool gets the text check in place of the exact form, as Bash does (Copilot's run_in_terminal is its shell).
  • Every other tool (a docs query, a coupon code, a Slack message) works, with every string of its input checked for protected paths, also percent-decoded (a file:// URL), and a string that looks like a path (a /, ~, or a file name with an extension) by where it really leads, from this folder and from the project folder (a link into a protected folder, or a new file in one). Such a string may not name the files that control the guards either (.mcp.json, Claude Code's settings, phiward's own files), since a local server could write them; a web address (https://...) and the input of a remote server may, since nothing here is written. A web address is still followed as a path (a local server may join it to its folder, where a link may be named https:). One that climbs above its host (https://x/../../f, https://../f, also percent-encoded), or one whose scheme names something in this folder or the project folder (a file or link https:), may not name those files either. A link made after the check (by a Bash call in the same turn), or in a folder the server joins paths to that is neither of these, is not seen. This check cannot be complete: the server may start from another folder, or a link may change after the check. Wrapping is the boundary. For a bare local server this text check is not a boundary: the server itself can read what you can. doctor names such servers; wrap the ones you use with protected data nearby.

docs.title: Which server a tool belongs to
docs.text:
Claude Code 2.1.274 and newer tells the hook each MCP tool's server and where its definition came from (mcp_server.source). phiward reads that scope's entry, by its exact name:

source phiward reads its tools local, project, user ~/.claude.json (this project's entry, or the top level) or the project's .mcp.json wrapped or remote: as such; else bare plugin the plugin's installed .mcp.json or plugin.json, in the copies that apply to this project (one installed for another project does not; a local or project copy before a user one); an entry of this plugin phiward cannot read makes it bare, other plugins' entries are not read wrapped (the plugin itself runs it under phiward launch) or remote: as such; else bare (phiward mcp wrap does not change a plugin's files: they are replaced on update) claudeai (a claude.ai connector) nothing remote sdk (the app's own servers, such as the desktop app's terminal) and any other source nothing bare

A server reached by URL counts as remote only when its URL surely names another machine; any URL phiward cannot read strictly counts as this machine. A server on this machine (an IDE's) runs outside Claude Code, so phiward cannot wrap it, and its command tools may make only gateway calls. A config entry phiward cannot read (args that is not a list of strings) counts as not wrapped, and does not change how the others are read. The detail: threat-model.md.

A config file of another scope cannot speak for the server, however it names it. With an older Claude Code (and with Copilot) the hook knows only the tool's name: then only your own config (~/.claude.json) can make a server wrapped or remote, and a server of .mcp.json counts as bare. doctor warns when Claude Code is too old. To see what your Claude Code sends, run bash tools/check-claude-mcp-source.sh from a phiward checkout (it runs claude -p once, in a temporary project, and changes no settings of yours).

docs.title: The repo config
docs.text:
.phiward.toml uses the same sections and keys, with the limits in Who may set what. An example:

[protected_paths]
roots = ["~/data/study-a"]

[sanitize]
packs = ["genomics"]

[git]
protected_branches = ["main"]

Do not rely on a repo config alone for protection: the agent can edit its repository. Put the roots that matter in the user config.

docs.title: Fail closed
docs.text: A config file that cannot be read, does not parse, has an unknown section or key, has a bad value, sets a key that is gone, or has a write_to entry that may not be granted, is a bad config. A repo config must also be a regular file, not a link, and not inside a protected path. With a bad config, every guarded action is refused until you fix it: the hook, phiward run and copy all refuse. phiward doctor prints the problem. For a repo config, the message the agent sees quotes nothing from the file (it may be a link into a protected folder); phiward doctor --show-paths, in your own terminal, shows why.

docs.title: Derived protected folders
docs.text:
When there is at least one protected path, two more folders are protected without being in the config:

  • the cache folder (it holds the gateway's scratch folders while commands run);
  • the .git of a work tree that holds a root (git keeps copies of its files there). The agent then cannot use git in that work tree. Keep protected data outside the repositories that the agent works in.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Set these in the shell where you start the agent tool and in the shell where you start the broker, with the same values. The Claude Code desktop app does not see variables you set in a terminal: for Mode A, keep the default places and do not set PHIWARD_CONFIG or PHIWARD_SPOOL (or set them in the env block of the Claude Code settings and for the broker service alike). doctor warns when the broker uses another config, cache folder or set of roots.

Variable Effect PHIWARD_CONFIG The user config file. Must name an existing file. XDG_CONFIG_HOME The base of the default user config place. XDG_CACHE_HOME The base of the cache folder. PHIWARD_SPOOL The broker's spool folder (default ~/.phiward-spool). PHIWARD_BROKER_WAIT Seconds a client waits for the broker to claim its request (default 10). PHIWARD_DEV 1: launch and install --user --write work from a source checkout, without phiward's check of its own installed files. For development only. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR Set by Claude Code for hooks. Without it, the hook cannot find the project settings, so it does not treat the shell as confined. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Claude Code's user settings folder (default ~/.claude). When it is set, Claude Code reads .claude.json (its user and local MCP servers) from it in place of ~/.claude.json, and so do mcp list, wrap, doctor and the hook.

The broker does not pass the agent's environment to gateway commands. A command gets only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, LANG, LC_*, TZ and TERM from the broker's own environment, and TMPDIR set to its private scratch folder.

docs.title: Daily use
docs.text:
• For: you, the operator, once phiward is set up.
  • You will have: a way to work with the agent on protected data, and an answer for each refusal.

The setup is in the quick start. The agent's own rules are the ones phiward init adds to your project's AGENTS.md (the text), and the skill.

How to ask the agent. Ask for counts and summaries of protected data, and let the agent run them through the gateway: for example "count the reads per sample in the protected folder with phiward run". The output comes back masked. Do not ask it to show records.

docs.title: Before the agent starts
docs.text:
1. The broker runs outside the agent: in a terminal of its own (phiward broker), or as a login service ((cd ~ && phiward broker --service --write), once).
  2. phiward doctor in the project's top folder shows no PROBLEM or WARNING line.

docs.title: Work with protected data: phiward run
docs.text:
phiward run -- samtools flagstat ~/data/patients/study-a/run1.bam

run is a client. It sends the words of the command to the broker, which runs the command in the gateway profile and sends back the sanitized output. The command:

  • can read every protected root;
  • can write only in its private scratch folder ($TMPDIR) and in granted folders (--write-to, from [broker] write_to; with one granted folder, it is the default and needs no --write-to). Protected roots are read only for it; a granted folder may sit inside a root;
  • has no network, unless --net is given and granted;
  • has an empty stdin and no terminal;
  • runs in the request's folder, with the broker's environment (not the agent's) and the program found on the broker's PATH (the PATH of the terminal that started the broker).

Every line it prints (stdout and stderr) goes through the sanitizer. A line longer than 64 KiB is withheld. At the end, run prints a note (when it has something to say) and one line. The note counts the placeholders in the lines shown, for example [placeholders in the lines shown: 412 <SAMPLEID>, 60 <BAMFILE>], and the lines the sanitizer withheld. From 20 shown lines on, when none holds an identifier placeholder (a subject, a sample, a patient's folder, an entry or a protected path), it says so: tell the operator, who checks [sanitize] packs and patterns with phiward doctor. Then run done: exit=0, or exit=1 when the command failed. The command's real exit status and the line counts go to the broker's log, which no session reads (a number the command chooses could carry data).

Write it as the whole command. Nothing before or after it: no cd, no pipe, no redirect, no $(...). The shell may expand globs, braces and ~. A gateway call in any other form is checked as an ordinary command: Claude Code's sandbox denies the protected paths to it, and where the sandbox does not confine the shell, the hook refuses it.

Write scripts that print aggregates: counts, summaries, tables. The sanitizer masks paths, entry names and identifiers. It does not mask other content. In text mode it also masks long numbers (<NUM>). --table reads CSV or TSV output by column: cells under an identifier header (sample_id, MRN, Patient ID, ...) show <IDCOL>, and numbers in the other columns are kept. It works only when the operator turned it on ([sanitize] table = true). One table per output: print its header as the first line, and give it an identifier column. When the first line is not such a header (a warning, a line of prose, a table with no identifier column), the whole output is masked as text. The first line that is not a row of the table (an empty line, a row with a quote or another field count, a row with no number, a second header) turns the rest into text: print one table per command. Under chrom and pos columns, both cells are shown (text mode masks chr1 1234567 as one <LOCUS>).

Exit codes: 0 when the command succeeded, 1 when it failed (whatever its own code); 2 for a refusal or a bad form; 3 for a config, sanitizer, broker or confinement problem; 127 when the program cannot start; 130 when it was cancelled.

Options (before --):

Option Effect --write-to DIR Also allow writes into DIR. DIR must resolve to a [broker] write_to folder of the user config, or a folder inside one. --net Allow the network. Needs [broker] net = true in the user config. --names-from FILE Also mask the names in FILE, an index file: tab-separated fields, where each field with a / is a path whose parts are masked (see configuration.md). Not a link, and inside a protected path. --table Read CSV/TSV output by column: cells under an identifier header are masked whole (<IDCOL>), numbers in other columns are kept; other lines are masked as text. Only when the operator set [sanitize] table = true.

Nothing asks the operator for a grant. A grant that is not in the user config is refused. The agent tool's permission mode does not change this.

A gateway command cannot read credentials or traces either: the same list that launch hides (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Kerberos tickets and keytabs, histories, other tools' logins, …). A command that needs one is not one for the gateway. This includes settings files that may hold a token: ~/.Renviron (R libraries set there are not found), pip and npm settings, ~/.m2/settings.xml, ~/.ipython, ~/.gnupg. Pass what a script needs as arguments, or set it in the script. On Linux the list is taken when the command starts: a credential made later is not hidden.

docs.title: Run a script the agent wrote
docs.text:
With choice 1 of phiward setup, gateway commands run only the listed programs: the @genomics tools, and the scripts in your scripts folder (the entry that ends in / in [broker] commands). So phiward run -- python3 summarize.py is refused: python3 is not listed, because it runs any code. To use a script that the agent writes:

  1. The agent drafts the script in the project, for example summarize.py, and tries it on made-up data.
  2. You read it. It must print only aggregates (counts, summaries, tables), never records, sample names or identifiers. Your reading is what keeps raw records out of the output: the sanitizer masks names and identifiers, not other content.
  3. Add a shebang as its first line (for example #!/usr/bin/env python3), and make it executable: chmod +x summarize.py.
  4. Move it into your scripts folder, for example mv summarize.py ~/pipelines/bin/. The agent cannot write there, so it cannot change the script after you read it.
  5. In your own terminal, run phiward pin: it approves the programs as they are now.
  6. Restart the broker; pin prints the command: (cd ~ && phiward broker --service --write).

Then the agent runs the script by its full path (the shell expands ~):

phiward run -- ~/pipelines/bin/summarize.py ~/data/patients/study-a

A changed script needs steps 2, 5 and 6 again. Until then, the broker refuses gateway requests, and phiward doctor names the program that is not approved. No scripts folder yet? Run (cd ~ && phiward setup) again, choose 1, and give one (keep it outside the projects the agent works in).

docs.title: Copy protected data: phiward copy
docs.text:
A copy never replaces a file that exists at the destination: it keeps it. To update a file, delete it yourself first.

phiward copy ~/data/patients/run1 ~/data/patients/run1-copy

copy SRC... DST copies without printing names. The destination must be inside a protected path of the user config, or under a [copy] remotes entry. Each local path is made absolute once, and every check and the copy itself use that path. One with a .. part, or one that starts with ~ (quoted, so the shell left it), is refused: give the full path. A local copy uses the system rsync -a (or cp -R). A copy to or from a remote is a tar stream through your shared SSH connection (hpc.md). The copy runs in the gateway profile and cannot read credentials. Its output is sanitized. The only option is --dry-run, as the first word: it counts what a push would send, and for a local copy it shows what rsync would copy.

docs.title: Give the agent pseudonymized data: phiward pseudonymize
docs.text:
When the agent needs a table but not its identifiers, make a copy in which the identifier columns hold codes. Type the command yourself, in your own terminal:

phiward pseudonymize --new-key labs --columns mrn --drop dob ~/raw/labs.tsv ~/data/patients/labs-coded.tsv
  • --new-key NAME starts a key; --key NAME extends it, so the same ID gets the same code in every table coded with that key. --prefix P (1 to 3 capital letters, default S) is fixed in a new key. A code is the prefix and 4 digits (S0042), drawn at random from the codes not used yet: a key holds at most 9999 IDs.
  • --columns H[=NEW],... names the columns to code. A coded column's header becomes NEW (default pseudonym, then pseudonym_2, ...). Every other column whose header looks like an identifier (the built-in list of phiward run --table and [sanitize] id_columns) must be named in --drop (left out) or --keep (kept as it is, on your word).
  • The kinds: the extensions decide, and the content must fit them. OUT has the same extensions as IN (labs.tsv.gz gives a .tsv.gz).
  • .tsv, .csv; .txt is read as a TSV and needs 2 or more columns (free text is refused).

  • .maf: a TSV after its # lines. Only the first #version line with a number (#version 2.4) is kept; the other # lines (commands, paths) are dropped, and a # line after the header is refused. Name the barcode columns, and keep the columns that look like IDs but are not:

    phiward pseudonymize --new-key samples --columns Tumor_Sample_Barcode,Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode \
  --keep Entrez_Gene_Id,Exon_Number ~/raw/cohort.maf ~/data/patients/cohort-coded.maf

    The command names each column that looks like an ID and is not named (by number): add it to --keep, or to --drop (Tumor_Sample_UUID).

    A coded MAF column keeps its header, so MAF tools still read the copy. Tumor and normal get unrelated codes. A free-text column (BAM_File) that names a sample is refused: drop it. - .vcf: the first line is ##fileformat=VCFv4.N. The IDs are the sample names after FORMAT, all coded, so give no --columns, --drop or --keep:

    phiward pseudonymize --new-key samples ~/raw/calls.vcf.gz ~/data/patients/calls-coded.vcf.gz
    • Of the ## lines only fileformat, INFO, FORMAT, FILTER and ALT are kept, and contig with its ID only (##contig=<ID=chr1>). The others are dropped: reference, source, fileDate, the command lines, SAMPLE, PEDIGREE. A kept line the sanitizer would mask is refused.
    • A sample name that is a word (tumor, normal, sample, sample1, control, germline, blood, unknown, na, none, in any case), has no digit or is under 3 characters is refused (also in another letter case or Unicode form, a full-width ｓａｍｐｌｅ1): it would link unrelated subjects in the key. Rename it first (bcftools reheader), or keep it as it is by number: --keep-samples 2 keeps the name of the second sample, out of the key, on your word. The only check of a kept name is that the sanitizer leaves it unchanged; a name it would mask is refused. A word with a digit (TUMOR1) is coded.
    • A short sample name of digits only (123) refuses every record that holds that number as a value: rename it first.
    • The records keep their order (tabix needs sorted positions) and their values. The sample columns are shuffled instead, the same in every record (--keep-order keeps them). A record or a kept line that holds a sample's ID (an INFO value, the ID column) is refused: clean it first (bcftools annotate).
    • The run reports the record count.
    • .json: the IDs are the values at the key paths you name. Keys are joined by ., and [] stands for every element of an array ([].mrn for an array at the top):
    phiward pseudonymize --new-key samples --columns 'samples[].id, samples[].mrn' \
  ~/raw/study.json ~/data/patients/study-coded.json
    • A key is matched exactly; a key with ., [ or ] cannot be named. A path that matches nothing, or meets a value of another kind (a key where there is no object), is refused.
    • A coded value is a string or an integer; it becomes a string code (9990001 and "9990001" get the same code, as in a table). null stays null. A true, a decimal number, an object or an array at a coded path is refused.
    • Every key that looks like an identifier and holds values (strings, numbers, true, false, null) is named by their path in --columns, --drop or --keep: samples[] for strings in an array under samples, samples[].id for the id of its objects. A key that holds only objects or arrays (samples above) needs no name. --keep names such a path; --drop names a key, and drops a container whole. A key the sanitizer would mask is refused: keys that are IDs are not coded.
    • The array at the last [] of a coded path (samples[] for samples[].id, an array of objects) is shuffled. It is refused when an array of the same length sits beside it in the same object: arrays side by side may be paired by position (samples and purity), and a shuffle would break the pairing without a word. Give --keep-order (it is for the whole run, never one array), or drop the other array. A path that ends in [] (ids[], the elements themselves) needs --keep-order: an array of IDs may be paired by position with arrays in other files. Other arrays and the order of keys are kept.
    • Refused as unreadable: a key twice in one object, NaN, Infinity, a number out of range (1e400), an integer of more than 4300 digits, nesting deeper than 100 levels, a lone surrogate (\ud800, which has no UTF-8 form).
    • Every key and every value of the copy is a field for the scan below; a number that is whole is also read as its integer (1234.0, "9.990001e6" for 9990001). The copy is written with an indent of 2, and it must read back as the coded document. A message names a key by its number in the order of the file. The run reports no count.
    • Each of them gzip-compressed (.tsv.gz, .maf.gz, .vcf.gz, .json.gz, .md.gz). Every member is read, up to 1 GiB expanded. The copy is plain gzip with no name and no time, and it must read back as the coded table before it is written. A bgzip (BGZF) input, every block of it, gives a BGZF copy; for a VCF, tabix -p vcf OUT indexes it. An index (.tbi, .csi) is never read or copied. A BGZF file must end with its EOF block (one cut short is refused), and a file that mixes BGZF blocks and plain gzip members is refused.
    • .md: the file holds only pipe tables and blank lines. The names of --columns, --drop and --keep apply to each table whose header holds them:
    phiward pseudonymize --new-key labs --columns mrn ~/raw/labs.md ~/data/patients/labs-coded.md
    • Each line of a table starts and ends with |, and the second line is the alignment row (| --- | :---: |). Any other line is free text and is refused: prose, a heading, a list, code, front matter, an HTML comment, a row without its outer pipes.
    • A line with a backslash or a backtick is refused: an escaped pipe (\|) or a code span has no safe split into cells. A line with <, [ or ] is refused: inline HTML, links, images and autolinks are not covered (write < for a <). A header with emphasis or an entity (**id**, _mrn_, patient_id) is refused: write it plain.
    • Two tables need a blank line between them: a row inside a table whose cells are all like --- is refused (it would read as a second header, coded as IDs). So is a body row of dashes only (| - | - |).
    • Each table follows the table rules: every column that looks like an identifier is named, in that table. Each name is found in some table, and one ID gets one code in all of them.
    • The body rows of a table with a coded column are shuffled (--keep-order keeps them); the other tables keep their order. The header and the alignment row are kept. The copy is written as | a | b | lines, one blank line between tables, and read back.
    • For the scan, every cell is also read with its HTML entities decoded (-, &#45;, ‐, also nested up to 4 times; deeper is refused) and its emphasis marks removed (**, _, ~~): FAKE-PT-0001 and 999**0001** are found. A message names a table by its number. The run reports the row count of all tables.
    • Not covered: Parquet; convert it to TSV with your own tools first.
    • A file that cannot be read or written as its kind gives one fixed refusal.
    • The rows are shuffled, so a file sorted by MRN does not give away the order of the IDs. --keep-order keeps the order.
    • The home folder itself is not a project (your ~/.claude is Claude Code's own folder), so an input in a folder of your home is taken; one below a project inside it is not.
    • The input is one table of those kinds (UTF-8, every row as wide as the header), reached with no link, outside every place an agent can write: the working folder and its git work tree, any project (a folder with .git, .claude or .phiward.toml above the input), the temp folders, the sandbox's allowWrite and additionalDirectories, a write_to folder, the spool and ~/.phiward. No field of the output (a cell, a header, the kept #version line, the codes too) may hold an ID of a coded column or of the key, also in another letter case, Unicode form, dash (‐, –, − and the other Unicode dashes) or script of digits, or escaped (%2D, \u002D, %E2%80%90, also escaped twice): an ID of 5 or more characters anywhere in a field, or across the fields of a line as written (Doe, John as the CSV fields Doe and John), and one with a letter also with every character but letters and digits removed (FAKE PT 0001, FAKE.PT.0001, FAKE-**PT**-0001 for FAKE-PT-0001; digits are never joined, so 999 0001 is not 9990001); one of 5 or more digits as a whole run of digits, so see 9990002 refuses and 19990001 does not; a shorter one with a letter as a whole word; a shorter one of digits only as the whole field. No field may hold an invisible format character. Not found: a short digit ID inside a cell (12 in 12 mg), an ID glued to other digits (19990001), an ID written another way (with spaces or other hyphens, 9 990 001), an ID with its leading zeros dropped or added (0001 and 1). Check such columns yourself, or drop them. Two IDs that are the same once normalized, as the scan reads them (P-1, p-1, a full-width Ｐ-1; FAKE%2DPT-0001, FAKE PT 0001 for FAKE-PT-0001; not FAKE-PT-00011), in the input or in the input and the key, are refused: make them one first. A key that already holds two such IDs cannot code either again: start a new key. The output is a new file of the same kind inside a protected root of your user config, outside every write_to folder. It is never replaced. The agent reads it through phiward run, masked; the codes pass the masks.
    • The key is ~/.phiward/backups/keys/NAME.tsv. No session, launch or gateway command can read or write it. It is only ever added to. phiward install claude makes ~/.phiward/backups; until then the command refuses. Keep a backup of the key where no agent can reach it: a lost key cannot be rebuilt, and new runs give new codes.
    • The command refuses without a terminal, and the hook refuses it as an agent command. Its messages name no value, header or path, and a run reports only the row count.

Never run it on a file the agent made or asked for, wherever it is, or with a key name the agent chose: the codes it gives would confirm the IDs the agent guessed. A file inside a protected root may have been put there by phiward copy at the agent's request; the command cannot tell. Run it from the folder of the project whose agent will read the copy: the places it refuses come from that project's sandbox settings (and the user's). Run it in a terminal the agent's app cannot read (not the app's own terminal panel): the command line you type, with its paths and headers, stays in the terminal's scrollback. What the codes do not hide is in threat-model.md.

docs.title: Check a command: phiward check
docs.text:
phiward check -- cat ~/data/patients/file.txt

check prints the hook's decision for a shell command in the current folder (allow, ask or deny) and the reason. The exit code is 0, 1 or 2. --cwd DIR before -- checks from another folder. check answers as if the command ran in Claude Code's sandbox. Where the shell is not confined, the hook refuses every command but a whole gateway call, whatever check says. It joins its words with spaces, so quoting in the command is lost.

docs.title: Filter your own output: phiward sanitize
docs.text:
some-producer 2>&1 | phiward sanitize

sanitize masks each line from stdin to stdout, with a sanitizer on: line before and a sanitizer done: line after. It does not list the roots, so it does not mask entry names (<ENTRY>); run does. Use it for output you share outside the agent. Options: --table, --names-from FILE, --check FILE and --check-table FILE (report whether a file would change), and --selftest (run the built-in test lines). --table and --check-table need [sanitize] table = true, read from the caller's own config: in this form that is a convenience, not a guard. Here --table reads no columns: each line is masked for identifiers only, and numbers and positions are kept. The hook does not accept this pipe form as a way to read protected data: use phiward run.

docs.title: When a command is refused
docs.text:
A refusal is a decision, not a fault. The reason says what to run instead. The agent must not try another spelling, a link, a nested shell, an encoded command or another tool to reach the same data. It also does not ask you to show it the data (! cat, a paste, a copy into the project) or to remove a guard. If it does, say no: that sends the data to the model provider.

Who acts on a refusal:

flowchart TD
  A["A command is refused"] --> B{"What does the reason name?"}
  B -->|"a protected path"| C["The agent: use phiward run or phiward copy"]
  B -->|"a credential or the hidden list"| D["Stop: ask the operator"]
  B -->|"the broker, the config, a grant or the program list"| E["The agent: use what is granted or listed; else the operator"]

docs.title: Refusals from the hook
docs.text: The hook refuses a tool call that names a protected path, and ends its reason with the rule: no tool may read, list, search or print a protected path; use phiward run -- CMD as the whole command, or phiward copy. Once a config exists, it also refuses phiward setup, broker, pin and carryover: those are for the operator only.

docs.title: Messages from run and copy
docs.text:
Messages start with run or copy (the table shows run; copy says the same), and the real text goes on with more detail. Four come from the broker itself and start with refused: (busy; cannot use this request; the config changed; programs not approved); all four exit with 3. An exit of 3 with no output at all means the broker refused the request before it could write anything: the broker's log has the reason.

Message Meaning What to do [... no identifier placeholder in the N lines shown ...] 20 or more lines were shown and no rule masked a subject, a sample or a protected name in them. If the data names subjects or samples, the operator checks [sanitize] packs and patterns (phiward doctor). run refused: no phiward broker is running No broker, or its heartbeat is older than 10 s. The operator starts the broker: phiward broker in a terminal, or the login service (setup.md §5). run refused: the request could not be written to the broker's spool folder The client cannot write the spool. The operator adds the spool folder to the tool's sandbox allowWrite (phiward install claude does it). run refused: the phiward config cannot be used A bad config. The operator runs phiward doctor (with --show-paths for a repo config, in their own terminal) and fixes the file. run refused: this program is not in [broker] commands of the config The operator lists the programs gateway commands may run. Use a listed program, or ask the operator to add yours; they restart the broker after. For a script the agent wrote, see above. run refused: no protected paths are configured The operator has not set phiward up yet. The operator runs cd ~ && phiward setup in their own terminal. run refused: --write-to names a folder that is not granted DIR is not a [broker] write_to folder or inside one (or is a link to somewhere else). Use a granted folder, or ask the operator to add one. run refused: --net is not granted [broker] net is not true. Work without the network, or ask the operator. run refused: the program is not on the broker's PATH The program is found neither on the broker's PATH nor as an executable path. Give the full path of the program (when a program list is set, only a program listed by its path or folder). Or the operator starts the broker again from a terminal where the program works (for example after conda activate). run refused: a write place is no longer a real folder A link was put on the path of a granted folder after it was checked. The operator checks that folder. run failed: the command could not start The program could not be started. Check the program and its path. copy refused: ... not under a configured remote A remote source or destination is not a [copy] remotes entry. Ask the operator to add the remote. copy refused: start your shared connection first … The shared SSH connection to the host is not running. The operator runs kinit, then ssh -fN HOST. refused: the broker cannot use this request (...) The request was malformed, or its folder does not exist. Run the command again from an existing folder. copy refused: a local path holds `..` or starts with `~` A local source or destination was written with .. or a quoted ~. Give the full path. copy refused: options are not accepted copy picks its own options. Remove the options (only --dry-run first is allowed). refused: the broker is busy Too many requests wait. Try again later. refused: the phiward config changed since the broker started The config, the approved programs or a names file changed while the broker ran. The operator reads the change and restarts the broker. refused: N program(s) of [broker] commands differ from what the operator approved A listed program changed, is new, cannot be read or is a link. The operator runs phiward doctor, checks the programs, runs phiward pin and restarts the broker. run refused: the sanitizer cannot start A pack, a names file or the entry limit is wrong. The operator runs phiward doctor. copy refused: the destination is not under [remote] roots of the user config ... A push goes only under a remote root, where remote output is masked. Ask the operator to add the folder to [remote] roots (phiward setup does it). copy refused: the destination is not inside a protected path of the user config A copy may not leave the protected folders. Copy into a protected folder, or to a configured remote. run stopped: cancelled The client was interrupted (Ctrl-C); the broker stopped the command. None. run stopped: the broker stopped before the command finished The broker went away. The operator restarts it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• doctor says the sandbox does not confine the shell. The reason follows. The usual ones: a root is missing from denyRead or denyWrite (run (cd ~ && phiward install claude --user --write) again after a config change), excludedCommands is not empty, a unix socket is allowed, an allowRead entry re-opens a root, or patterns are configured. (Inside Claude Code, the hook also needs $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; Claude Code sets it.) The hook then refuses shell commands other than gateway calls, doctor and check. With [shell] best_effort on, the hook checks shell command text instead, which is best effort (configuration.md).
  • doctor says the broker uses another config. The broker and the agent tool were started with a different HOME, PHIWARD_CONFIG or XDG_* variable. Start both from the same environment.
  • A write place is skipped. doctor says why: it does not exist yet, or a link is on its path. Name the real folder in write_to.
  • A gateway command fails to write to /tmp. The gateway sees /tmp read-only. It writes temporary files to $TMPDIR, its private scratch folder.
  • git does not work in a repository. A protected root sits in that work tree, so its .git is protected. Move the data out of the repository.
  • Every shell command fails after an upgrade. An older phiward's shell prefix is still set: run (cd ~ && phiward install claude --user --write) again (doctor warns about it).

docs.title: For contributors: how phiward decides
docs.text:
• For: a contributor who changes phiward's own code.
  • Before: a checkout of the repository, python3 3.9 or newer, and uv for the tests.
  • You will have: a working setup that touches nothing of your own, and a picture of how a decision is made.

phiward keeps protected health information (PHI), and the credentials that would reach it, out of what an AI coding agent sends to its model provider. The rules for a change are in CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md. This page does not repeat them.

docs.title: The first half hour
docs.text:
Work beside your own setup, never in it. You may use phiward for real work, with a real config and a running broker. Three variables point a checkout away from them. The tests set the same ones (tests/conftest.py).

Open a new terminal in the checkout, and close it when you are done:

SCRATCH="$(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && pwd -P)"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/fakehome" "$SCRATCH/phi" "$SCRATCH/repo"
echo SECRET-CONTENT-0001 > "$SCRATCH/phi/FAKE-PT-0001.bam"
printf '[protected_paths]\nroots = ["%s/phi"]\n' "$SCRATCH" > "$SCRATCH/fakehome/phiward.toml"
export HOME="$SCRATCH/fakehome" PHIWARD_CONFIG="$SCRATCH/fakehome/phiward.toml"
export PHIWARD_SPOOL="$SCRATCH/spool" PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src"
python3 -m phiward doctor
  • HOME is a scratch home. PHIWARD_CONFIG names a made-up user config. PHIWARD_SPOOL names a scratch spool. doctor must name your scratch config, not your real one.
  • Never run setup, install, pin, carryover or broker --service against your real home. Never run the real claude in an experiment.
  • python3 -m phiward broker in this terminal is a scratch broker. A second terminal, with the same SCRATCH and the same exports, can then send it python3 -m phiward run -- CMD. Do not type a bare phiward here: that is your installed release, not the checkout. launch refuses a checkout unless PHIWARD_DEV=1 is set.

Run the tests in a normal terminal (they make their own scratch home). The command, and how to run a part of the suite, are in tests/README.md. For one file, add its path: tests/test_protected_paths.py.

Try a decision by hand. check shows the decision for a shell command. Nothing runs:

python3 -m phiward check --cwd "$SCRATCH/repo" -- cat "$SCRATCH/phi/FAKE-PT-0001.bam"

It prints deny: and the reason. The exit status is 0 for allow, 1 for ask and 2 for deny. check judges the command as if Claude Code's sandbox confined it.

The hook itself reads a payload on stdin. Feed it a made-up one:

printf '{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s/phi/FAKE-PT-0001.bam"},"cwd":"%s/repo","permission_mode":"default"}' \
  "$SCRATCH" "$SCRATCH" | python3 -m phiward hook claude; echo "exit=$?"
Reply Meaning exit 0, no output allow exit 0, a JSON object with "permissionDecision": "ask" on stdout ask: Claude Code shows a prompt exit 2, phiward [protected-paths]: ... on stderr deny, with the reason exit 2, phiward: the hook could not decide ... on stderr a fault: it is refused too

The payload above is denied. With "tool_name":"Write" and the path $SCRATCH/repo/.vscode/tasks.json you get the ask. A Bash payload is refused here: a hand-made payload has no $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and no settings in the scratch home confine the shell.

docs.title: What the agent controls, and what phiward trusts
docs.text:
The agent controls (never trusted) Trusted (the operator's) the hook payload, its cwd included the user config, and pinned.toml next to it the project folder, and a repo .phiward.toml in it the other guard files (config.guard_files): the broker's status file, phiward's own install the temp folders the broker, and the environment it builds for a command every file in the spool the operating system's sandbox the words and the folder of a gateway request Claude Code's sandbox and permission rules (Mode A)

A repo .phiward.toml can only add protection. Everything that widens the gateway comes from the user config (configuration.md).

The invariants. Each one has a place in the code:

  • Fail closed. A guard that raises denies (core.dispatch). A hook fault exits 2 (adapters/claude.main). A config that cannot be used refuses what it guards.
  • The strictest answer wins: deny over ask over allow (core.strictest). An ask that the tool cannot show becomes a deny (core.settle).
  • A new check only adds refusals. It never changes what kind of action a tool is, and never turns a refusal into an ask (review-rounds.md).
  • What is checked is what starts. The gateway runs the entry of the user config's list, not a path the agent names (run.listed_run_path). pin records each listed program by its content. The broker refuses every request when the config or a listed program changed since it started (broker.config_print).
  • Nothing asks the operator at run time. Grants come from the user config only.
  • Made-up data only, in tests and in experiments (FAKE-PT-0001).

docs.title: One tool call
docs.text:
Claude Code runs phiward hook claude before each tool call (Mode A).

sequenceDiagram
    accTitle: One tool call through the hook
    accDescr: Claude Code sends a payload. The adapter makes an Action. decide judges the confinement. The guard returns a Decision. The adapter replies.
    participant CC as Claude Code
    participant H as claude.main
    participant T as claude.to_action
    participant D as adapters.decide
    participant G as protected_paths.check
    CC->>H: PreToolUse payload on stdin
    H->>T: the payload
    T-->>H: an Action
    H->>D: the Action
    Note over D: loads the config and judges the confinement of a shell call
    D->>G: core.dispatch: the Action and the config
    G-->>D: a Decision
    D-->>H: the strictest Decision
    H-->>CC: allow, ask or deny
    Note over CC: its sandbox enforces at run time, after the hook
  1. adapters/claude.to_action turns the payload into an Action (core.py): the kind (shell, file read, file search, file write, other), the folder, the command or the paths, and whether the session can show an ask. No policy lives here.
  2. adapters.decide loads the config for the action's folder. For a call of Claude Code's own shell tools, it checks that Claude Code's settings confine the shell. This is where the sandbox comes in: the hook does not run the sandbox. It records confined on the Action, or the reason why not.
  3. core.dispatch runs every guard and keeps the strictest decision. Today there is one guard, guards/protected_paths.check.
  4. check judges the action by its kind. Read the function for the order of its checks: the order changes, and each step says why it is where it is.
  5. claude.main writes the reply of the table above.

Under phiward launch (Mode B) the kernel decides. The hook there is a quick first layer (fasthook.py).

docs.title: One gateway request
docs.text:
phiward run -- CMD is a client only. The broker runs the command, outside the agent.

flowchart TD
    accTitle: One gateway request
    accDescr: The client leaves a request in the spool. The broker claims it, checks it, runs the command in a kernel profile, masks the output and writes the reply.
    A["phiward run -- CMD<br/>the client, in the agent's sandbox"] --> B["req-ID.json in the spool"]
    B --> C["The broker claims it<br/>renames it to job-ID.json"]
    C --> D{"Config unchanged,<br/>listed programs approved?"}
    D -- "yes" --> E["run.execute<br/>config, grants, [broker] commands"]
    D -- "no" --> R["A refusal message"]
    E -- "not granted, not listed" --> R
    E --> F["CMD in the kernel profile<br/>confine.gateway_command"]
    F --> G["The sanitizer masks each line"]
    G --> H["out-ID.log, then done-ID.json"]
    R --> H
    H --> I["The client prints the output"]
  • The request holds the words and the folder, and no environment. The broker builds the command's environment from a short list of its own variables (broker.command_env).
  • The broker treats every file in the spool as untrusted data (the top of broker.py says how).
  • run.execute loads the user config plus the repo config of the request's folder. It checks the grants (--write-to, --net) and [broker] commands.
  • run.run_confined starts the command in the profile that confine.py builds. The command reads the protected roots. It writes only its scratch folder and the granted folders. It has no network unless granted.
  • Every line goes through sanitize.Sanitizer. Masking hides names and identifiers, not other content. With --table, sanitize.Columns reads the lines by column (fresh for each call).
  • The agent sees exit=0 or exit=1 only, and a note that counts the placeholders in the lines shown (run_confined). The real exit status and the counts go to the broker's log.
  • phiward copy and phiward run --remote take the same road (copying.execute, run._execute_remote).

The list in modes.md. install then writes new rules, and the hook refuses the shell until they are in place: say in the changelog that users wire again a tool name (a new Claude Code tool) the tool sets at the top of adapters/claude.py, and to_action a message the user sees the table in daily-use.md; tests/test_v2_refusal_words.py a help text USAGE in cli.py and the module's own HELP a new test file the index in tests/README.md (a test checks it)

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
The words that phiward's pages use, in alphabetical order.

  • Broker: the program that runs gateway requests outside the agent, as you, and masks what comes back. You start it (best as a login service: phiward broker --service --write). The agent cannot start or change it.
  • Carry-over, trusted copy, quarantine (Mode B only): each phiward launch session starts from a trusted copy of the agent tool's settings, skills and MCP servers, which you fill with phiward carryover add. What a session changes there goes to quarantine. Nothing from quarantine is used until you accept it (phiward carryover accept).
  • Config: phiward's own settings, a TOML file (~/.config/phiward/config.toml, written by phiward setup): your protected roots, grants and the like. Not Claude Code's settings; those are the wiring. See configuration.md.
  • Confined: a shell, or a program, whose reads the kernel limits (Claude Code's sandbox, or phiward's kernel profile). The hook refuses every command of a shell that is not confined but a whole gateway call.
  • Derived protected folders: folders that phiward protects without being in your config: its own cache folder, and the .git of a repository that holds a protected root.
  • Gateway: phiward run, phiward copy and phiward run --remote. The only way the agent works on protected data. The broker runs each request and masks the output.
  • Gateway call, whole command: a phiward run -- CMD or phiward copy written as the entire command, with fixed words: no cd X && before it, no | head or > file after it, no $(...) or variable. Only that form runs where the shell is not confined.
  • Grant: a capability you give the gateway in your own config. write_to lets a gateway command write in a folder; net lets it use the network. The default is none. Nothing asks you at run time: what the config does not grant is refused.
  • Hidden list: credentials, Kerberos ticket caches and keytabs, SSH keys, shell histories, other logins and the like, which no agent may read, in addition to your protected roots.
  • Hook: a command that Claude Code runs before each tool call (phiward's guard) or when a session starts (phiward's note on the rules).
  • Kernel profile: a set of rules that the operating system enforces on a program and every program it starts (on macOS Seatbelt; on Linux bubblewrap, seccomp and Landlock). The program cannot switch them off. Mode B runs the whole agent tool in one.
  • Masking: the gateway replaces protected paths, file names and identifiers in output with placeholders such as <PROTECTED>. It does not hide other content, so print counts and summaries, not records. The part of phiward that masks is the sanitizer.
  • MCP server: a program that gives an agent tool more tools (Model Context Protocol). phiward has one, phiward mcp, whose tools are the gateway.
  • MCP server: wrapped, not wrapped, remote: a wrapped server runs under phiward launch --, in the kernel profile, so it cannot read protected data. A not wrapped one (shown as "not wrapped (runs with your rights)") can read what you can; its tools that run commands may make only gateway calls. A remote one runs on another machine and nothing here. phiward mcp list says which each of yours is. See modes.md.
  • Mode A: a normal Claude Code session (the desktop app, an IDE or a terminal), wired by phiward install claude. Claude Code's own sandbox and permission rules, plus phiward's hook, keep protected data out. See modes.md.
  • Mode B: the whole agent tool run under phiward launch, in phiward's kernel profile. Terminal only. See launch.md.
  • Operator: you, the person who installs phiward and owns the config. The agent's rules use this word.
  • Pack: a built-in or own list of identifier patterns to mask (for example genomics).
  • Plugin: a bundle of hooks, skills, commands and MCP servers that Claude Code installs in one step. See plugins.md.
  • Protected root: a folder whose contents the agent may not read. You list them in your config.
  • Remote Control: a Claude Code feature that lets you drive a session that runs in a terminal from the desktop app, the web or a phone.
  • Scope, source (MCP servers): where a server's definition lives. Your own user scope (~/.claude.json), this project's local entry in it, the repository's project file (.mcp.json), or a plugin. Claude Code tells the hook each tool's source (2.1.274 and newer); an older one does not, and then a .mcp.json server counts as not wrapped.
  • Shared SSH connection: one SSH connection to a cluster that you open yourself (ssh -fN hpc). phiward's HPC requests join it through its control socket, so they need no key or ticket of their own. See hpc.md.
  • Skill: written guidance that an agent loads when it needs it. phiward's skill tells the agent how to work through the gateway.
  • Spool: the folder where the agent leaves requests for the broker (~/.phiward-spool).
  • Wiring: what phiward install claude writes into Claude Code's settings: the hooks, the sandbox rules and the permission rules. User wiring (--user) covers every session in every folder; project wiring covers one project.

docs.title: HPC: Kerberos, mounts, copy and run --remote
docs.text:
• For: people whose agent runs on their own computer (a Mac in the examples), in a Claude Code session (Mode A) or under phiward launch (Mode B), and who reach an HPC cluster with a Kerberos ticket and a shared SSH connection (kinit, then ssh -fN).
  • You will have: the agent working with HPC through the gateway, with masked output.

Use one host name everywhere: the Host in your ~/.ssh/config, the Host in phiward's ssh config, [remote] hosts, and the host part of [copy] remotes. ControlPath ~/.ssh/cm-%C matches only when HostName, User and Port are the same in both ssh configs.

The rule: the agent may work with HPC, but protected data reaches the model only masked. Hence two paths:
